topStories.headline: Marion County Heads to the Polls Tuesday — Here's What's on Your Ballot
topStories.dek: Election Day is November 3, with two Marion County school-levy renewals, four county races, a statewide voter-ID amendment, and a U.S. Senate special election all on the Marion County ballot.
topStories.body:
Marion County voters have a full ballot waiting for them when polls open Tuesday, November 3. At the top of the ticket is a competitive U.S. Senate special election alongside Ohio's governor's race and five other statewide offices. Locally, Marion County residents will choose among candidates for County Auditor, County Commission, County Coroner, and a Family Division Common Pleas judge.

The statewide measure drawing the most attention is Issue 3, a legislative constitutional amendment that would require voters to present a government-issued photo ID to vote in person, with a photo ID or a signed alternative identifier required for absentee ballots. A majority yes vote would enshrine the requirement in the Ohio Constitution.

Two school-levy renewals appear on Marion County ballots. Ridgedale Local Schools is asking voters to renew a 2.44-mill levy for five years, and Elgin Local Schools has a 2.88-mill renewal on the ballot for the same period. Both are renewals, not new taxes. Voters can confirm which questions appear in their specific precinct by contacting the Marion County Board of Elections at 222 W. Center St.

In-person absentee voting continues today, Friday October 30, from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., then on Saturday October 31 from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Sunday November 1 from 1 to 5 p.m. On Election Day itself, polls open at 6:30 a.m. and close at 7:30 p.m. Absentee ballots must be received by the board no later than 7:30 p.m. on November 3.

topStories.headline: OSU Marion Launches Free Three-Part Storytelling Workshop Open to All Community Members
topStories.dek: Ohio State Marion announced this week a no-cost community workshop called 'Your Story, Well Told,' with applications due November 6 and the first session set for November 16.
topStories.body:
The Ohio State University at Marion announced on October 28 that it is offering a free three-part storytelling workshop open to any community member who wants to discover, develop, and share their own personal narrative. The program, titled 'Your Story, Well Told,' is funded by the Marion Community Foundation and is part of the America 250 celebration marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

The workshop will be led by Dr. Jennifer Schlueter, Dean and Director of Ohio State Marion. Applications are due November 6, with the first session starting November 16. Community members interested in participating can find details at osumarion.osu.edu.

The program builds on a thread of community storytelling work at the campus. Earlier this spring, Ohio State Marion hosted 'Who We Are Now: A Celebration of Marion, OH,' a live performance that wove together stories from local residents. Organizers noted at the time that memories gathered during that event would inform a larger performance planned for the Marion Palace Theatre in December 2026.

topStories.headline: Bucci's Italian Scratch Kitchen Named 2026 Heritage Ohio Main Street Business of the Year
topStories.dek: The downtown Marion restaurant occupying a historic 1920s trolley depot has earned the state's top Main Street business honor for 2026.
topStories.body:
Bucci's Italian Scratch Kitchen, the scratch-made Italian restaurant at 320 W. Center St. in downtown Marion, has been named the 2026 Heritage Ohio Main Street Business of the Year, according to Downtown Marion, Inc. The award is among the most prestigious recognitions available to businesses in Ohio's Main Street program network.

Bucci's operates out of the former Columbus, Delaware and Marion Electric Railway freight and passenger depot, a 1920s building that had fallen dormant before the restaurant opened. Chef John Paul Iacobucci built the menu around authentic family recipes with a strict made-from-scratch approach, covering soups, entrees, house-made sauces, and desserts. The restaurant also operates an event and wedding venue within the same historic space.

The Heritage Ohio honor follows another major recognition from earlier in the year: the U.S. Chamber of Commerce named Bucci's one of the top 100 small businesses in the entire country in its 2026 CO—100 list, chosen from more than 12,000 applicants nationwide. Bucci's is open Tuesday through Thursday 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m., Friday 11:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., and Saturday 4 to 10 p.m.

moreNews.headline: PUCO Winter Reconnect Order in Effect Through November 1
moreNews.body: The Public Utilities Commission of Ohio's annual Special Reconnect Order is currently active, allowing Ohio utility customers who are behind on bills to restore service for a capped reconnect fee. The City of Marion posted notice of the order on October 6, 2026. The SRO expires November 1; residents with questions should contact their utility provider or visit marionohio.us.

moreNews.headline: Marion Public Library 'Reading Marion Monuments' Program Launched Oct. 26
moreNews.body: The Marion Public Library began a two-session public program called 'Reading Marion Monuments' on October 26, meeting at Marion Veterans Park to help participants interpret the symbols, scale, materials, and placement of war memorials and public monuments. A second session follows in early November. Registration details are available at the library's main desk, 445 E. Church St.
